> 小過。亨，利貞。可小事，不可大事。飛鳥遺之音，不宜上，宜下，大吉。

Hexagram 62 is about a small overshoot, and both characters in its title need rescuing.

## 過 is 度 — to pass

說文: 過，度也 — to pass through, to go across.

Extended: to cross over, to exceed.

So 小過's 過 is going a little past, not committing a fault. The whole hexagram is about one inch out of position, not about crime.

That distinction has to be made first, because the whole tone of the chapter depends on it. Nothing in 小過 is dramatic. Everything in it is slightly too far.

## 飛鳥遺之音

遺: to be gone, to be left behind (說文 遺，亡也).

A flying bird leaves its sound.

And the reading has to be exact: not "the bird leaves a sound as it flies." It is: the bird has gone, and the sound is still there.

Which explains the next clause: 不宜上，宜下.

The sound goes up and the person is gone from sight; the sound comes down and it reaches the ground.

So the hexagram's advice is a piece of acoustics: whatever is left of you after you have gone should be falling, not rising. The bird itself is not the subject. Its residue is.

## 妣

妣: a deceased mother (說文 妣，歿母也). 祖 is the father's line above; 妣 is the grandmother who has died.

六二: 過其祖，遇其妣；不及其君，遇其臣，無咎.

Passing the grandfather and meeting the grandmother; not reaching the ruler and meeting the minister.

Two overshoots and two arrivals in one line, and the verdict is no fault — because every miss landed on something. Which is the chapter's better side: the small overshoot is survivable when what you hit is still the right kind of thing.

## 弗過防之，從或戕之

Nine-three: not overshooting, but defending; and if one follows, one may be killed.

戕: to kill (說文 戕，槍也; one gloss, a subject killing his lord from another state is called 戕).

Which is the hardest line in the hexagram: the failure here is not going too far. It is not going quite far enough — not overshooting — and then, following along, being cut down.

So 小過 does not simply say "stay small." It says the smallness must still be a position that can defend itself.

## 弋

弋: an arrow with a cord (說文 弋，橜也; the shooting sense is one of its primary uses).

Shot out, and it can be pulled back. So what it takes is limited.

六五: 密雲不雨，自我西郊；公弋取彼在穴.

Dense clouds, no rain, from my western suburb; the duke shoots with a corded arrow and takes what is in the cave.

The same 密雲不雨 as 小畜卦辭 — the clouds have gathered and nothing has come down. And the response is a corded arrow into a hole: a small instrument reaching into a small place. Which is exactly what 小過 permits.

## 灾眚

Top line: 弗遇過之，飛鳥離之，凶，是謂灾眚.

眚: an eye disease, a film growing over the eye (說文 眚，目病生翳也), extended to a fault one brings on oneself.

And this distinction matters: 灾 comes from outside, 眚 is self-inflicted.

The top line has already been sentenced 凶, and then the text adds 是謂灾眚 — which means: this is not a disaster that fell on you. You put a film over your own eye.

## The test

Take a place where you are slightly out of position — a role one size too big, a comment one notch too sharp. Ask the hexagram's question: after you have gone, is your sound falling or rising? And nine-three's: does the small position still defend itself, or is it only small?
